=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/claude_issue_route.py:1080-1113 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The `recent` counter in `env_requeue_decision` tallies every trusted requeue marker in the rolling window regardless of which blocker they reference. When blocker #1 exhausts its two retries in 24h and a new environment failure (blocker #5, different reason) appears on the same issue, `recent` already equals `max_retries` and the new blocker is immediately alerted without its own retries.
  WHY: This is not a crash or data-loss. The issue still gets an alert, and a human can comment `/reclarify`. The spec says "at most 2 per issue per 24h," so this is per-spec. But it can surprise operators who would expect a genuinely new failure class to get a fresh allowance.
- scripts/claude_issue_route.py:984 | severity=NIT | confidence=1
  PROBLEM: The `<!-- ai:claude-blocked:v1 -->` marker gains an optional `reason=<reason>` suffix inside the same HTML comment. Every existing reader that matches on the `<!-- ai:claude-blocked:v1` prefix still matches the reason-extended form.
  WHY: N/A — no break confirmed by test.
- scripts/claude_issue_queue_watchdog.sh:160-163
  PROBLEM: The `gh_retry gh api -X POST "repos/${SELF_REPO}/dispatches" --input "${dispatch_file}"` call sends a repository_dispatch to coding-workflows. If the intake workflow is temporarily broken (e.g., a clone of the dispatch body is malformed), the dispatch succeeds but the intake fails silently.
  WHY: The watchdog has no way to know whether the intake succeeded until the next hourly run. Suggested minimal fix: Add a comment documenting that dispatch success does not guarantee intake success, and that the intake failure path (Telegram alert from `claude_issue_intake.sh`) is the primary signal.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
